bodySections.heading: Why timing matters
paragraphs: This cat fvrcp plan sequences doses against calicivirus outbreaks, not against a vague “sometime this season” intention for your cat.

Milestone labels on the cat fvrcp table (8 weeks; 12 weeks; 16 weeks; Annual or risk-based) are operational deadlines for daycare, boarding, travel, and multi-pet intros — a nearly finished cat fvrcp kitten series is still incomplete.

If your household also wrestles with panleukopenia in rescues or assuming one kitten shot is enough, put those constraints on the same calendar thread as the FVRCP booster so one reminder system owns the cat fvrcp week.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Call the clinic with product names and prior dates the day you notice a missed cat fvrcp dose; catch-up timing depends on age and gap length for this cat scenario.
Until the cat fvrcp series is current again, reduce the exposure pattern that matches calicivirus outbreaks, and do not wait for an annual wellness slot to ask about a cat fvrcp make-up dose.
After the visit, enable 7-, 3-, and 1-day nudges for the next FVRCP booster due date so the same cat fvrcp miss cannot hide inside a shared family calendar.

faqs.question: Is this cat FVRCP vaccine schedule a prescription?
faqs.answer: No. It is an editorial planning table aligned with common AAHA/AAFP-style windows and facility patterns. Your veterinarian sets the legal and medical plan for the individual cat.

faqs.question: What if we already missed a date on this cat fvrcp schedule?
faqs.answer: Contact the clinic for catch-up timing. Bring prior records, limit high-risk exposure tied to calicivirus outbreaks, and reset reminders as soon as the next cat fvrcp due date is known.
